necessary_context.content: For arbitrary A in R^{m×n}, one query chooses v in R^n and returns Av, OR chooses u in R^m and returns A^T u. Each product costs one; both cost two; b vectors cost b. Queries are measurable adaptive functions of the transcript and independent private seed. Computation and storage are uncharged. Output is any transcript-measurable rank-k orthogonal right projector P in R^{n×n}.
necessary_context.name: Oracle and output

necessary_context.content: N=min(m,n), 1≤k<N. OPT_{p,k}(A)=min over rank-k orthogonal P_* of ||A(I−P_*)||_{S_p}. Success means ||A(I−P)||_{S_p}≤(1+epsilon)OPT_{p,k}(A). Schatten-p is the l_p norm of singular values; p=infinity is their maximum. Q_p^* is the least integer q giving success probability at least 2/3 on each input with at most q queries on every input and every seed realization. This is an all-path cap, not expected cost.
necessary_context.name: Loss and minimax convention

necessary_context.content: For fixed input size all random variables lie in standard Borel spaces; the seed belongs to the transcript sigma-field. Conditional Gaussian laws hold for almost every realized transcript. Tildes suppress polylogarithms in dimension, rank, norm parameter and inverse accuracy. Fixed-p constants may depend on p; uniform results for p≥2 have universal constants. Lemma 4.2 instead has any fixed positive success probability under the Gaussian input distribution.
necessary_context.name: Conditional laws and constants
